title: He copied nothing, because there was nothing to copy
subtitle: Al-Badi': the Originator of the heavens and earth without any prior model
intro: Al-Badi' (الْبَدِيعُ) means the Incomparable Originator: the One who brought the heavens and the earth into being with no earlier model, no sample and no precedent, and whose work is astonishing in its beauty. When He decides a thing, He says Be, and it is. Nothing in your life is too new or unheard-of for Him.

root.sense: The root means to start something with no example before it. A badi' thing is unprecedented and wondrous, the kind of work that makes people stop and say: nothing like this has ever been seen. Al-Badi' is the Originator of a creation that had no pattern to follow.

knowing: When someone brings out a truly original invention, crowds gather around them. They read their life story, queue for their product, and treat them almost with reverence, all for something assembled from metal and glass that was already in the world, built on the ideas of others. {idea}Al-Badi' originated the whole universe with no material, no earlier idea and no example{/idea}. He is not the first to do it well; He is the first, full stop.

This is what separates Al-Badi' from Al-Khaliq. Al-Khaliq speaks of measuring and bringing into being; Al-Badi' speaks of the utter newness of what He made. Everything human creativity produces borrows from His creation. The engineer copies the bird; the architect copies the honeycomb. He copied nothing.

And it costs Him nothing. In both places the Quran uses this name, it ties it to His complete independence: He only says to a thing, Be, and it is (2:117), and He has no son and no partner, for He created all things (6:101). {reward}The One who needs no model also needs no help{/reward}.
seeing: Both verses that name Him Al-Badi' answer the claim that Allah has a son (2:116-117, 6:100-101). The reasoning is beautiful: the One who originated the heavens and earth from nothing has no need of offspring, a partner or a helper. A creator who needs a family is a creature. Al-Badi' is above that.

Yusuf, at the end of his long story, called on Allah as Fatir, the One who split open the heavens and the earth into being (12:101), when his dream finally came true. The boy in the well, the slave, the prisoner, now reunited with his family on a throne: no one could have predicted that path. {reward}Al-Badi' writes stories no one has read before{/reward}.
trusting: We often judge what is possible by what we have seen. No one in my family has done this. No one recovers from this. No one gets out of this kind of debt. {trap}That thinking quietly limits Allah to precedent{/trap}. Al-Badi' made a universe without one. A way out that has never been seen before is no harder for Him than one that has.

So when you ask Him, do not ask small. Ask the One who said Be to the heavens and earth for the cure, the reconciliation, the opening that seems unheard of. Then do your part and leave the how to Him; He does not need your plan as a model either.
loving: Wonder is one of the doors to love. Snowflakes that never repeat, sunsets that are never the same twice, a newborn's face: Al-Badi' fills the world with first-time beauty. {reward}A heart that keeps noticing His originality keeps falling in love with Him{/reward}, because it never gets used to Him.
now: The specialist closes the file and says gently that cases like yours are rare, and there is no standard path. You walk out into the car park feeling like there is no map. Remember that the heavens and earth had no map either. Al-Badi' does not need a precedent to open a way for you.
old: If something has never happened before, I assume it cannot happen to me.
new: Al-Badi' originated everything without precedent, so nothing is impossible because it is new.
try: Write down one thing you stopped asking Allah for because it seemed unheard of, and ask Him for it again tonight, by this name.

dua.text: Ya Badi' as-samawati wal-ard, You made the heavens and the earth with nothing before them. Make for me a way out that I cannot yet imagine.
dua.note: A well-known supplication recorded by Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i calls on Allah as Badi' of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of majesty and honour.

pairs.why: Al-Khaliq is about measuring and bringing into being; Al-Badi' adds that it was done with no earlier pattern.
Al-Mubdi' begins creation for the first time; Al-Badi' highlights how new and wondrous that beginning is.
The endless variety of forms by Al-Musawwir shows the originality of Al-Badi'.

faq.a: Al-Badi' means the Originator who creates without any previous model or example. It also carries the sense of wondrous beauty, since what He makes is new and astonishing. The Quran calls Him Badi' of the heavens and the earth.

faq.q: Where is Al-Badi' mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: Allah is described as Badi' as-samawati wal-ard, Originator of the heavens and the earth, in 2:117 and 6:101. Both verses connect the name to His independence: He says Be and it is, and He has no son or partner.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Badi' and Al-Mubdi'?
faq.a: Al-Mubdi' is the One who begins creation the first time, in contrast to Al-Mu'id who repeats it. Al-Badi' stresses that His creation had no model and is wondrous in its newness. One is about the beginning, the other about its originality.
